deferred_material.latex:
\begin{remark}[The central sign still acts on transformation laws]\label{hyperbolic.central-sign}
The matrices $g$ and $-g$ give the same transformation, but their denominators $cz+d$ and $-cz-d$ have opposite signs. For example, suppose a complex-valued function satisfies
\[
 f(\gamma\cdot z)=\chi(\gamma)(cz+d)^k f(z),\qquad
 \gamma=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},
\]
for an integer $k$ and a character $\chi$ of a subgroup containing $-I$. Substitution of $-I$ gives $f(z)=\chi(-I)(-1)^k f(z)$, so a function that is not identically zero requires $\chi(-I)(-1)^k=1$. With the trivial character this forces $k$ to be even. This calculation explains why the geometric action may pass to $\operatorname{PSL}_2$ while a transformation law must still remember the chosen matrices. The automorphy factor, its cocycle identity, and the slash action will be developed in \hyperref[v1a-ch03]{the chapter on holomorphic modular forms}.
\end{remark}
